name: Housing and Homelessness
description: Affordable housing reporting, senior facility sales, and multi-family housing funding.
summary: The citywide homelessness and affordable housing reporting ordinance O2026-0024022 was held in committee on 2026-04-08 [9], then passed committee on 2026-05-13 [10] and City Council 50 Yea / 0 Nay on 2026-05-20; it repeals Sections 2-44-070 and 2-50-085, adds Section 2-4-130, and shifts the annual homelessness report from DFSS/DOH under now-defunct USICH principles to the Mayor's Office of Homelessness under the Five-Year Blueprint, with reports due to the Committee on Housing and Real Estate each August 31 [1][3]. The sale and transfer of the Heritage Woods senior living facility at 2800-2822 W Fulton St and 300-326 N California Ave to High Point Residence Chicago West Realty LLC (affiliated with Vantage Senior Care) passed committee as a substitute on 2026-07-08 [11] and City Council 49 Yea / 0 Nay on 2026-07-15, with the 113-unit supportive living facility keeping all non-manager units at 50% AMI and about $3.3 million in City debt repaid at closing [5]. Multiple multi-family funding ordinances passed City Council with 50-0 or 49-0 tallies: SO2026-0024073 (HUB32, 2026-04-15), O2026-0024884 and O2026-0024885 (3959 N Lincoln Ave, 2026-05-20), O2026-0025467 (Abrams Intergenerational Village, up to $3.25 million multifamily and $13 million TIF, 2026-06-17) [6], and O2026-0028750 (Harvest Homes II, 2026-10-14). A 2026-07-08 subject matter hearing on the Flexible Housing Pool by the Center for Housing and Health took no vote [11], and public comment that day urged full funding of the pool and opposed a renters/rental registry ordinance pending a forensic audit of housing spending [4]. A 2026-01-14 briefing on the Five-Year Blueprint on homelessness presented point-in-time count data and plans to work with the CTA on overnight stays, with no vote recorded [2]. Still open are Flexible Housing Pool funding and any action on the rental registry concerns raised in comment [4][11].
one_line: Council shifted homelessness reporting to the Mayor's Office, approved Heritage Woods sale and several multifamily funding ordinances; Flexible Housing Pool funding remains open.
